system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's Updated SPA Positions and Disclosure Letter

I've reviewed the Seller's package against our playbook. It departs from our positions in numerous material respects — and several of these are dressed up as "agreed," "settled" or "for administrative simplicity" when they are nothing of the sort. Per our playbook sec 0.4/6.3, I've treated none of the Seller's characterisations as binding. Here are the material issues.

---

## 1. General liability cap (Clause 12.1) — PUSH BACK

**Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
**Playbook:** Open at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is a *conditional fallback* usable **only** with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft — and **none has been given**.

This is the trap. The Seller's number happens to match our fallback figure, but a position is not cleared merely because a number coincides (sec 6.3). We must open at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do **not** concede 20% unless and until Amelia Frost gives written, draft-specific authority.

## 2. Thresholds (Clause 12.2) — PUSH BACK HARD

**Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery (only amounts above the basket recoverable).
**Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; seller liable **from the first dollar** once the basket is exceeded.

Three separate departures, each adverse: the de minimis is 5x ours, the basket is 5x ours, and the "excess above the basket" mechanic (a deductible, not a tipping basket) is contrary to our first-dollar position. Reject all three.

## 3. Time limits (Clause 12.3/13) — PUSH BACK

**Seller:** 18 months; and a sweep clause making "any limitation... apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
**Playbook:** 24 months general; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost approval (**none given**).

Same trap as the cap — 18 months matches our fallback but is not cleared. Open at 24 months. Separately, the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" sweep is a hidden general-regime override that would swallow the Fundamental/Title and fraud carve-outs. Reject it; limitations must be expressed category-by-category.

## 4. Fundamental / Title conflated into general regime — REJECT

**Seller:** capacity and title warranties to carry the **same caps and time limits** as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."

This is the most aggressive move in the package. Our playbook requires a **separate** Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to subordinate title and capacity protection to a 20% cap and 18-month cut-off. Insist on the standalone fundamental regime and keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate (no hidden override).

## 5. Fraud / wilful misconduct — ABSENT, MUST BE ADDED

The Seller's Clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance to **"all Claims of any nature"** with **no carve-out** for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct.

Our playbook is non-negotiable here: fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one may waive this. Add an express carve-out overriding 9.3/12.8/20.5.

## 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2]) — REJECT deemed disclosure

**Seller:** general/deemed disclosure of the **entire data room** (DD-002 to DD-012) plus **public registers** and the Accounts/statutory registers.
**Playbook:** require specific, fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.

Reject [1.1] and [1.2] wholesale-disclosure sweeps. Require disclosure to be fair and specific — identifying the matter with sufficient detail to enable assessment. Note [1.4] also pre-emptively denies that any consent/payment/notice/remediation is "legally required" — fine as a non-admission, but it must not cut down our warranties.

## 7. Buyer knowledge (Clause 8.3) — REJECT blanket exclusion

**Seller:** no claim for any matter the Buyer **or its advisers** knew, **including anything discoverable from the data room or public records**.

This is a blanket buyer-knowledge/constructive-knowledge bar — exactly what our playbook says to delete. "Discoverable from the data room or public records" is constructive/imputed knowledge, which we reject. Any knowledge qualifier must be limited to the **actual** knowledge of **named** buyer individuals, and must **never** excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. Delete 8.3 and replace narrowly if at all.

## 8. Bluefen consent (Clause 3/6.3) — PUSH BACK

**Seller:** "reasonable endeavours" and treat consent as satisfied **on delivery** of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure para 2 confirms **no** final consent and **no** evidence conditions (clause 11.3) are satisfied.

Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m) — a material customer. Our playbook requires **effective** consent **and** evidence its conditions are satisfied **before Completion** — not consent-on-delivery, and reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer. Make effective Bluefen consent (with condition evidence) a Completion condition.

## 9. Riverlark (Clause 2/7) — PUSH BACK

**Seller:** release "following Completion." Disclosure para 3: ~AUD 3,200,000 still outstanding, **not repaid**, **no discharge** of security included.

Our playbook requires current payout figure, **direct repayment from Completion funds**, and **effective security releases** at Completion. A post-completion release is acceptable *only* with an irrevocable undertaking **plus** Amelia Frost approval (none given). Insist on direct repayment and release at Completion; this also bears on the debt-free/cash-free mechanics.

## 10. Employee bonuses (Funds flow / DD-005) — PUSH BACK

**Seller:** AUD 420,000 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and **not itemised** in the funds flow; on-costs (payroll tax/super) unaddressed.

Our playbook: the DD-005 AUD 420,000 **plus triggered on-costs** must be a specific line item **or** seller-funded, and the funds flow must not silently exclude them. The Seller "not itemising" them is precisely the silent exclusion we must prevent. Require either explicit seller funding or a dedicated funds-flow line item, including on-costs.

## 11. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1) — PUSH BACK

**Seller:** indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment, "considered adequate." Disclosure para 4: DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, **not independently verified**; no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment; DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 materials on **cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**.

Broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure (transfer on cleared payment). The AUD 180,000 is **not independently verified either way** — don't accept it as settled in either direction. The risk is we don't get the SOW3 Project Materials if fees are unpaid; the indemnity must cover that broader exposure.

## 12. Export/privacy incident (Clause 4.6 / DD-006) — PUSH BACK on characterisation

**Seller:** "preliminary operational matter... not expected to be material."
**Facts (para 6):** download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); unknown whether anyone accessed it, unknown scope, unknown whether notification required.

Our playbook: assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand **in either direction**. So resist both the Seller's "not material" spin *and* any assumption of a crystallised breach. Require: preserve logs, complete the investigation, and ongoing updates. Do not let the Seller use "preliminary" to disclaim the warranty/indemnity coverage of whatever the investigation reveals.

## 13. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000) — ASSESS, don't accept labelling

**Seller:** "ordinary-course operating costs." Disclosure para 8: three renewals AUD 110,000 each; silent on whether each is unavoidable/terminable/accrued/ordinary course.

Our playbook: assess; **no automatic Debt classification or price deduction** — but equally don't accept the Seller's "ordinary course" label at face value. We need to understand timing, terminability and whether any are accrued liabilities before agreeing treatment.

## 14. Title (Clause / Disclosure para 10, DD-012) — PUSH BACK

**Seller:** title "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012."

DD-012 is a **supplied internal source**, not independent proof (our playbook says exactly this). Require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence. Note para 10 itself concedes it "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification" — so we must.

## 15. Tax / IP — NOT settled

**Seller:** tax and IP "settled under the general regime above."

Our playbook: Tax and IP terms remain **OPEN**; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution. Reject the assertion that folding them into the (defective) general regime settles them. Keep them as separate, open categories.

## 16. Other disclosure items noted

- **Office lease (para 7):** notification obligation only — the material does *not* make it a landlord-consent condition. Fine, but confirm the notification is handled; don't let it migrate into a consent CP.
- **Mossvale (para 9):** restriction on assignment that, per the disclosure, does *not* require consent merely on a share sale. Verify this reading against DD-009 ourselves.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our action |
|---|-------|-----------------|------------|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / 4.8m | Open at **25% / 6.0m**; 20% needs Frost written authority (none given) |
| 2 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k / excess-only | **5k / 50k / first-dollar** tipping basket |
| 3 | Time limit | 18 months + sweep clause | **24 months**; delete "applies to all Claims" sweep; 18m needs Frost (none given) |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Merged into general | **Separate regime**: 100% cap, ≥6 yrs, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge |
| 5 | Fraud carve-out | Absent | **Add** carve-out from all caps/baskets/limits/exclusive remedy/non-reliance |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data room + registers | **Specific fair disclosure only**; reject deemed/constructive |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket + constructive | **Delete**; at most actual knowledge of named persons; never title/capacity/fraud/indemnity |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours / consent-on-delivery | **Effective consent + condition evidence as Completion CP** |
| 9 | Riverlark | Release post-Completion | **Direct repayment + release at Completion**; deferral needs undertaking + Frost |
| 10 | Bonuses | Not itemised | **Seller-funded or explicit funds-flow line item**, incl. on-costs |
| 11 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3-only | **Broaden**, preserve SOW3 cure; 180k unverified either way |
| 12 | Export incident | "Not material" | Preserve logs, investigate, updates; **no assumption either way** |
| 13 | Sandbar | "Ordinary course" | **Assess**; no auto Debt/price deduction, but no auto acceptance either |
| 14 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent** title/encumbrance/authority evidence |
| 15 | Tax/IP | "Settled" | **Remain open**; reject folding into general regime |

**Two priority traps to flag to the deal team:** (a) the cap (20%) and time limit (18m) match our *fallback* numbers but are **not cleared** — they require Amelia Frost's written, draft-specific authority, which has not been given; and (b) the "same caps/time limits for Fundamental/Title... for administrative simplicity" plus the "applies to all Claims" sweep are a coordinated attempt to collapse our separate protective regimes and omit the fraud carve-out. Hold the line on both.

**Authority check:** Before we concede anywhere near 20% / 18 months, or agree any post-Completion Riverlark release, we need Amelia Frost's written sign-off identifying this draft. Nothing in the Seller's "agreed/settled" labelling substitutes for that.

Want me to turn this into a mark-up of the specific clauses, or a one-page issues list for Amelia Frost to action the authority points?
=== END ADVICE ===
